title: Load a caulking gun (one hand holds its release down, the other pulls the rod back) and seal a bath joint
instruction: Load the caulking gun and seal the joint between the bath rim and the tiles: with one hand press the gun's release lever down and keep it pressed while the other hand pulls the plunger rod back by its hook, all the way out; let go of the lever, lay the white cartridge from the tray in the gun's cradle with its nozzle through the front yoke, and push the rod back in until its plate meets the cartridge. Then lift the gun with both hands, put the nozzle's tip into the joint and run it along the joint from one end to the other, laying a bead of sealant. Put the gun back on its grip and rest block, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Plumbers, tilers and decorators load and use caulking guns many times a day. The gun's plunger rod is held by a ratchet that lets it come back only while the release is held down, so loading it takes two hands: one on the release, which also steadies the gun, and one pulling the rod.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) An empty caulking gun lying level along the table, its nozzle end to the left, its cradle's axis 30 cm forward and 9 cm above the table: a red powder-coated steel frame (0.40 kg) with an open half-round cradle 5.6 cm across and 23.6 cm long, from a back plate 2 cm left of the centre line to a front yoke 25.6 cm left with a V notch for the nozzle; a black rubber pistol grip under the back plate, its foot on the table, and a red steel trigger; the front of the cradle rests on a pine rest block 6 cm wide, 4 cm long and 6 cm tall. (2) The gun's zinc-plated steel plunger rod (0.10 kg, 8 mm thick) with a 4.2 cm push plate inside the cradle, 8 cm in front of the back plate, and a D-shaped hook (4.4 cm long, 4.4 cm tall, 1 cm wide) at its back end, 17.6 to 22 cm right of the centre line. (3) The gun's zinc-plated steel thumb release lever on top of the frame behind the back plate, its ribbed pad 3 cm wide, 13 cm above the table, between 0.6 cm right and 1.6 cm left of the centre line. (4) A cardboard tray 10 cm wide and 34 cm long, its middle 17 cm forward and 13.5 cm left, with two notched cardboard saddles; on them, lying along the table with its nozzle to the left, a new 300 ml cartridge of white silicone sealant (0.30 kg): a white polyethylene tube 4.9 cm across and 20.5 cm long with a blue and yellow label, and a translucent nozzle 12 cm long, already cut, its middle 17 cm forward and 13 cm left. (5) The white acrylic rim of a bath, 10 cm tall, from 14 to 48 cm forward and from 39 to 43.2 cm left, against (6) a wall of white ceramic tiles (7.5 cm square, grey grout) rising 30 cm from 43.2 cm left. The unsealed joint is the corner where the rim's top meets the tiles, from 18.5 to 37.7 cm forward. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The rod is held by a ratchet: it slides into the gun freely but back out only while the release lever is pressed down at least 6 degrees. The cartridge is seated when it lies in the cradle nozzle first: its axis within 8 mm of the cradle's middle sideways and within 1 cm of where it lies in the cradle up or down, pointing within 8 degrees of the gun's axis with its nozzle toward the yoke, and its shoulder at most 3 cm short of the yoke. The rod is in against it when the push plate is within 4 mm of the cartridge's back end. A bead is laid along each of the joint's twelve 1.6 cm lengths that the nozzle's tip passes over while the cartridge is seated with the rod in against it and the tip is within 1.5 cm of the joint, sideways and up or down. The gun is back on its rest when it lies within 2.5 cm of where it started, tilted no more than 6 degrees and turned no more than 8 degrees. At the end: 1.0 with the cartridge seated, the rod in against it, a bead along at least 10 of the 12 lengths, the gun back on its rest and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5 with the cartridge seated, the rod in against it and a bead along at least 6 lengths; 0.25 with the cartridge seated; else 0.0. A bead once laid stays laid. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the gun, the rod and the cartridge still.
reset_notes: Wipe the bead off the joint, take the cartridge out of the gun and lay it back on its tray, push the rod back in until its plate is 8 cm in front of the back plate, and lay the gun back on its grip and rest block.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the ratchet is a spring drive on the rod's slide that the task file locks against backward travel unless the lever is pressed; the trigger is not modelled, and the bead is laid by rule (white segments placed along the joint) where the loaded gun's nozzle tip passes. The rim, wall, tray and rest block are fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
